a frame ten frames (0.33s0.33\text{\,}\mathrm{s}) after the reference frame of case S2 (Table5).
Both panels show the same zoomed-in crop of the3840×21603840\times 2160frame, centered on the largest
moving group; orange boxes
are the vehicles that moved together between the two frames, with their motion. The estimate
registers the group back onto where it stood (capture fraction0.960.96), so its error, drawn
as black arrows on a grid and magnified by the factor in the legend, carries the platoon’s motion
across the whole crop (10.0px10.0\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x}corner error against the reference estimator), while23%23\text{\,}\mathrm{\%}of its466466inliers
lie on the moving vehicles (orange dots). The same pipeline under oriented-box masks (right)
keeps783783inliers, none on those vehicles, at a corner error of0.9px0.9\text{\,}\mathrm{p}\mathrm{x}. Both are re-registered
with the stored parameters and seed of the real-time campaign (Section7.3).

Figure 2:Part I. A scene frame is warped by a known geometric and photometric perturbation, and
the pipeline registers the warped copy back onto the original. The perturbation is the ground
truth, so no separate reference estimate is involved. The object annotations enter twice and for
different purposes: as the feature mask handed to the pipeline, and as the object boxes whose
object-level errors are scored.

Figure 3:One trial of the detector campaign, registered again
with the campaign’s stored parameters and seed. (a) The evaluation scene with the most objects,
everyOBBoutlined. (b) Its perturbed copy in trial 0, with the sampled parameters above it and
a random sample of unmasked ORB’s inlier matches drawn between the two frames. (c, d) The dashed
crop of (a) with every ORB inlier unmasked and underOBBmasks, the masked area (eachOBBscaled about its center by1+m1+m,Table2) shaded; orange marks an inlier on an
annotated object, blue one elsewhere. Nothing in the scene moves, so the inliers on vehicles are
correct here; under masking ORB spends that share of its feature budget on the
ground.

Figure 4:Accuracy against compute on the tuning scenes, at the
untuned starting thresholds. Each panel is one pipeline; a line joins the downsampling ratios0.180.18,0.300.30,0.500.50and1.01.0at one feature budget (color and marker),
unmasked (solid) or underOBBmasks (dashed), so a split between the two lines is a masking
effect. A circle rings Part I’s operating point (1.01.0,80008000features), a square
Part II’s offline one (0.500.50,20002000features) and a diamond its real-time one, the
cheapest point of the grid (0.180.18,10001000features). Time is the median registration time
per frame pair; mAA is drawn on a logarithmic scale of1−mAA1-\text{mAA}, so the last hundredths
before saturation stay visible. LoFTR has no point at full resolution, which exceeds the benchmark
GPU’s memory.

Figure 5:Part II. Every candidate registers the same frame pairs under each masking mode in turn,
and the reference estimator registers them once, underOBBmasks. The reference
estimator supplies pseudo-ground truth and its own error is measured againstGCP; that residual is the equivalence margin of the reference-relative pixel metrics. On the audited frames a homography fitted
to the same points is an independent reference of its own, and the identity transform is scored on
every pair as the unstabilized baseline. The object annotations enter as the feature mask and,
placed by the reference estimator, as the evaluation region and as the object motion that the
capture fraction is read against.

Figure 6:The nine cases ofTable5at their reference
frames, in cell order. Every object annotated in the reference frame is outlined by itsOBBand colored by what it did2222frames later, the longest offset the survey reads: displaced
with the largest group that moved together, displaced otherwise, found where it was, or not found.
Objects are found again as the survey finds them, with the reference estimator’s transform as the
platform motion, as for the capture measure (Section4.5); arrows are
displacements at true scale, and each panel counts the objects found, displaced and moving
together; the low-moving cases show few displaced objects by definition. Each panel is one pair, whereas the survey’s descriptors average five offsets and remove
the platform motion by an affine fit to the background.

against its time offset, pooled over the cases at each audited offset (box: quartiles and median;

Figure 8:The capture fractionλ\lambda(Eq.18) of every real-time
measurement on a pair with a moving group, against the offset: one panel per pipeline, its title
counting the captured measurements, and a marker per masking mode. The dashed line is the capture
threshold of0.10.1and the shaded band the survey’s offsets of11to3131frames.
The axis is linear within the threshold and logarithmic beyond it, so a partial pull, a complete
capture (λ≈1\lambda\approx 1) and a breakdown far from zero are all visible. The offline regime
is inFig.1, the captured share per offset bin inFig.2.

Figure 9:The offline counterpart ofFig.1: the captured unmasked measurement of the
offline regime with the largest capture fraction within the survey’s offsets of11to3131frames whose registration reproduces its stored estimate, beside the same pipeline underOBBmasking, drawn as inFig.1.

Figure 10:Inlier ratio against the disagreement with the reference estimator, offline (top) and
in real time (bottom). In each row, left, the density of frame pairs and pipelines, one panel per
masking mode, darker where more of them fall, on a logarithmic scale of the count; right, the
Spearman coefficient between the two within each pipeline and case, one point per group, with
the median printed beside it and the number of positive coefficients under each masking mode.
A negative coefficient means that a higher inlier ratio goes with a smaller
error.

Figure 11:Every candidate in the offline (top) and real-time (bottom) regime, pooled over the nine

broke down (Section7.3). Full rows inTables8,9,10and11.
